players.product: hyperscale data-center leases (>1 MW, 300+ data centers, 1.4 GW under construction) and 0-1 MW colocation / interconnection on PlatformDIGITAL

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 results (CFO): Core FFO of $2.04 per share, up 15% year-over-year, helped by data center leasing, development-related lease commencements and higher fee income from the strategic private capital platform; Same-Capital Cash NOI up 7.9% year-over-year (2.5% on a constant currency basis, held back by a low operating-expense comp); Debt to Adjusted EBITDA fell to a multiyear low of 4.7x and the FFO Payout Ratio fell to 64%.
quarterly_data.figure: Core FFO $2.04 per share (+15% YoY); Same-Capital Cash NOI +7.9% (2.5% constant currency); leverage 4.7x

quarterly_data.signal: Second highest bookings quarter in company history and the strongest leasing start to a year: leases signed representing $707 million of annualized rent at 100% share or $423 million at Digital Realty share, nearly 70% above the next highest quarter; the Americas were over 75% of DLR-share bookings and APAC set a quarterly record. The 0-1 MW plus interconnection product posted a record $98 million of signings (a 40%+ increase versus first quarter 2025, third quarterly record in the past year), with a record 21% of 0-1 MW bookings AI-oriented requirements, 116 new logos, a record 1-3 MW leasing band, and interconnection bookings of $18.6 million (24% higher than a year ago).
quarterly_data.figure: $707 million signed at 100% share / $423 million DLR share; 0-1 MW + interconnection $98 million (21% AI-oriented); 116 new logos; interconnection $18.6 million (+24%)

quarterly_data.signal: Signed the largest single lease in Digital Realty history: a 200 MW AI inference-oriented lease with a double-A-rated hyperscaler in Charlotte (the company's first hyperscale deployment in that market, delivering in phases starting next year into 2028, which stretched the sign-to-commence lag). Also signed 10+ MW leases in each of Dallas, Sao Paulo and Tokyo; greater-than-1 MW signings exceeded the prior three quarters even excluding the record lease, Americas greater-than-1 MW leasing was $280 million, and pricing averaged $181 per kW. CTO Chris Sharp: demand has converted from pilot to production, the 200 MW build is inference, and agents are a demand multiplier representing 5-30x more tokens per task. Hyperscale contracts run 15 years with escalators of 3% or higher.
quarterly_data.figure: 200 MW AI inference lease (largest in company history); >1 MW Americas leasing $280 million; $181 per kW; 15-year hyperscale contracts, escalators 3% or higher

quarterly_data.signal: Total backlog reached a new record of $1.8 billion at the end of the first quarter, or $1 billion at Digital Realty share, as $423 million of new bookings exceeded $204 million of commencements; $544 million of leases are scheduled to commence somewhat ratably through 2026, $247 million in 2027 and $242 million in 2028 and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: backlog $1.8 billion (100% share) / $1 billion DLR share; $544 million commencing 2026, $247 million in 2027, $242 million 2028+

quarterly_data.signal: Development pipeline scaled more than 60% from year-end to approximately $16.5 billion at 100% share, with 1.2 GW under construction, 61% pre-leased at an 11.4% average expected yield; nearly 80% of the volume is in the Americas driven by AI-oriented workloads from the largest customers. In Q1 the company delivered 63 MW of new capacity (84% pre-leased) and started about 464 MW (nearly 50% pre-leased). Charlotte and Atlanta eclipsed Dallas and Chicago as development markets (Northern Virginia remains largest); a second 200 MW building will follow the first in Charlotte and construction launched on another 200 MW site in Atlanta (2028 delivery). CEO: roughly 3 GW is operating today plus another 6 GW owned, of which 1.2 GW is under construction.
quarterly_data.figure: $16.5 billion under construction (up more than 60%); 1.2 GW, 61% pre-leased, 11.4% yield; 63 MW delivered, 464 MW started; ~3 GW operating + 6 GW pipeline

quarterly_data.signal: Capital spending: $910 million of development CapEx in the quarter, net of partner share; 2026 CapEx net of partner contributions raised by another $250 million at the midpoint to a range of $3.5 billion-$4 billion. Funding: finished the $3.25 billion U.S. hyperscale data center fund in March, leaving approximately $10 billion to support hyperscale development, plus incremental dry powder in the $8+ billion hyperscale development joint venture; $500 million-$1 billion of dispositions and JV capital planned later in the year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 development CapEx $910 million; 2026 CapEx $3.5 billion-$4 billion (+$250 million); $3.25 billion hyperscale fund

capex.period: 2026 plan (net of partner contributions, as of Apr 2026)

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 guidance raised: Core FFO per share range raised by $0.10 to $8-$8.10 per share, a midpoint representing 9% growth over 2025; cash renewal spreads now expected at 6.5%-8.5% (up 50 basis points); occupancy still expected to improve 50 basis points-100 basis points from year-end 2025; Same-Capital Cash NOI growth of 4%-5% on a constant currency basis. Q1 renewals: $193 million at a blended 5% cash increase ($157 million of colocation renewals at 4.3%; $32 million of greater-than-1 MW renewals at a 74% cash spread). CFO expects a step down in Q2 Core FFO, rebounding in Q3.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 Core FFO $8-$8.10 per share (+$0.10; 9% growth at midpoint); renewal spreads 6.5%-8.5%; Same-Capital Cash NOI 4%-5%

quarterly_data.signal: Land and market expansion: acquired an 873 acre parcel in the Greater Atlanta Metro expected to support a 1 GW data center campus (power alternatives still being worked through with the power company) and a 30 acre Hillsboro parcel expected to support 160 MW of IT capacity, adding to an 85 MW assemblage there; entered Milan, Sofia (acquisition of Telepoint) and Cyberjaya, Malaysia, with land in Portugal. About 275 MW in Northern Virginia not yet leased is poised for 2027-2028; capacity is being prepared in Dallas, Hillsboro, Sao Paulo, Frankfurt, Paris, Tokyo, Osaka and Seoul.
quarterly_data.figure: Atlanta 873 acre parcel for a 1 GW campus; Hillsboro 160 MW (plus 85 MW); ~275 MW unleased Northern Virginia capacity for 2027-2028

quarterly_data.signal: Industry constraints: CEO says power availability, labor and supply chain risks and community concerns are widening the gap between theoretical demand and deployable capacity, with competition over supply chain, shortages of skilled electricians and utility partner delivery delays; build cost per megawatt is rising with land values, supply-chain tightness and a shift to higher-priced designs with more liquid cooling, yet market rent growth is still outpacing build-cost inflation, keeping close to 11% unlevered returns. CTO: the High-Density Colocation program can retrofit to 150 kW a rack. Energy: approximately 90% of utility expense is reimbursed by customers, and most of the rest is hedged forward through 2026 and beyond.
quarterly_data.figure: up to 150 kW a rack (High-Density Colocation); ~90% of utility expense reimbursed; close to 11% unlevered returns
